# Deficiency diseases (beriberi, rickets, pellagra, goitre, night blindness) (`vitamins_deficiency`)

<!-- generated by scripts/build_techtree.py from techtree/core/medicine.yaml — do not edit -->

- Category: Medicine & hygiene (`medicine`)
- Deps: helped by controlled_trial, scurvy_citrus, nixtamalisation, epidemiology_mapping
- Core idea: Some diseases come from something missing in the food, not from a germ or a poison. Replacing the missing nutrient can reverse some symptoms; severe or longstanding deficiency can leave permanent damage. Beriberi (weak legs, heart failure) strikes people living on polished white rice: eat unpolished rice, the bran, beans or meat. Rickets (bent bones in children) can result from a shortage of vitamin D or calcium; limited sunlight increases the risk of vitamin D deficiency. Pellagra (rough skin, diarrhoea, madness) follows a diet of maize that was not treated with lime: add meat, milk, beans, or prepare maize the Mesoamerican way. Iodine deficiency can cause goitre and impair fetal brain development; iodised salt helps prevent it. Vitamin A deficiency is one cause of night blindness; vitamin A-rich foods help prevent that deficiency.
- Pitfalls:
  - Looking for a germ or a spoiled-food poison; this delayed the answer to beriberi and pellagra by decades
  - Giving more of the same poor food instead of a different food
  - Sunning children behind glass or fully clothed, which does nothing against rickets
  - Overdosing: too much liver or fish-liver oil poisons, and iodine doses must be tiny
  - Presenting vitamins as a cure for diseases in well-fed people
- History: egypt: c. 1550 BC – Ebers papyrus prescribes liver for an eye disease usually read as night blindness; china: c. 340 – Ge Hong recommends seaweed for goitre; 7th c. Sun Simiao describes beriberi and treats goitre with animal thyroid and seaweed; americas: from c. 1500 BC – lime treatment of maize protects Mesoamerican peoples from pellagra; 1914–1915 Goldberger proves pellagra dietary; 1924 iodised salt in Michigan; 1937 Elvehjem identifies niacin; east_asia: 1884 – Takaki Kanehiro ends beriberi in the Japanese navy by changing the ration; 1897 Eijkman (Batavia) produces it in chickens fed polished rice; 1901 Grijns reads it as a deficiency; europe: 1650 – Glisson describes rickets; 1735 Casal describes pellagra in Spain; 1820 Coindet treats goitre with iodine; 1912 Hopkins and Funk state the vitamin idea; 1919–1922 Mellanby, Huldschinsky and Chick show cod-liver oil and light cure rickets; 1922 iodised salt in Switzerland
- Read:
  - Casimir Funk, The etiology of the deficiency diseases, Journal of State Medicine (1912)
  - Joseph Goldberger, The Etiology of Pellagra: The Significance of Certain Epidemiological Observations with Respect Thereto, Public Health Reports (1914)
  - Kenneth J. Carpenter, Beriberi, White Rice, and Vitamin B (2000)
